title: In Space, Fire Burns as a Blue Ball

scenes.text: In space, fire burns as a floating blue ball.
On Earth, hot air rises, which stretches a candle flame into a teardrop.
On the space station, nothing rises. The flame has no up.
So it grows evenly in every direction into a sphere.
It is also blue, because the soot that makes flames yellow is missing.
NASA studies these flames to understand how fire really works.

description:
In microgravity a flame is spherical, soot-free and blue, because there is no rising hot air to stretch it.
NASA runs fire experiments on the space station to understand fire and soot.
What else would act strangely in space?
first_comment: On Earth the yellow in a flame is glowing soot. Did you know that?
